{{Short description|Category whose objects are small categories and whose morphisms are functors}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically in [[category theory]], the '''category of small categories''', denoted by '''Cat''', is the [[category (mathematics)|category]] whose objects are all [[small category|small categories]] and whose [[morphism]]s are [[functor]]s between categories. '''Cat''' may actually be regarded as a [[2-category]] with [[natural transformation]]s serving as [[2-morphism]]s.

The [[Initial and terminal objects|initial object]] of '''Cat''' is the ''empty category'' '''0''', which is the category of no objects and no morphisms.<ref>[https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/empty+category empty category] at nLab</ref> The [[Initial and terminal objects|terminal object]] is the ''terminal category'' or ''trivial category'' '''1''' with a single object and morphism.<ref>[https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/terminal+category terminal category] at nLab</ref>

The category '''Cat''' is itself a [[large category]], and therefore not an object of itself. In order to avoid problems analogous to [[Russell's paradox]] one cannot form the “category of all categories”. But it is possible to form a [[Glossary of category theory|quasicategory]]<!-- Note the article [[quasicategory]] is about different notion. --> (meaning objects and morphisms merely form a [[conglomerate (mathematics)|conglomerate]]) of all categories.

==Free category==
{{Main|Free category}}
The category '''Cat''' has a [[forgetful functor]] ''U'' into the [[quiver category]] '''Quiv''':

:''U'' : '''Cat''' → '''Quiv'''

This functor forgets the identity morphisms of a given category, and it forgets morphism compositions.  The [[left adjoint]] of this functor is a [[functor]] ''F'' taking '''Quiv''' to the corresponding [[free category|free categories]]:

:''F'' : '''Quiv''' → '''Cat'''

==1-Categorical properties==

* '''Cat''' has [[Complete category|all small limits and colimits]].
* '''Cat''' is a [[Cartesian closed category]], with [[Exponential object|exponential]] <math>D^C</math> given by the [[functor category]] <math>\mathrm{Fun}(C, D)</math>.
* '''Cat''' is ''not'' locally Cartesian closed.
* '''Cat''' is [[locally presentable category|locally finitely presentable]].
